albums.blurb: Kottke recorded this solo acoustic set for John Fahey's Takoma label in 1969, when he was 24 and still largely unknown; it is popularly called the Armadillo album after the animal on its cover. Its fourteen short pieces of driving, polyphonic steel-string fingerpicking, most of them on 12-string, extended the American primitive style Fahey had pioneered, and it remains the best-known record of Kottke's long career.
albums.reception: It has reportedly sold more than half a million copies, making it one of the best-selling solo acoustic guitar albums ever released.

albums.blurb: The London singer and guitarist's third album arrived on Nonesuch in July 2020, five years after Blood, and was the first she produced herself, working with Matt Hales, Beni Giles, and Mura Masa. Its ten songs, nine originals plus a cover of Radiohead's "Weird Fishes," trace the arc of a relationship from bloom to breakup in her guitar-led blend of neo soul and folk.
albums.reception: The album holds a Metacritic score of 83 out of 100 from 19 critic reviews, in the site's "universal acclaim" band.

albums.blurb: L'Impératrice ("The Empress") is a Paris six-piece founded in 2012 around keyboardist Charles de Boisseguin and fronted by singer Flore Benguigui, working in string-swept disco-funk sung mostly in French. Tako Tsubo, their second album, followed the 2018 debut Matahari on the microqlima label and takes its title from takotsubo cardiomyopathy, the "broken-heart syndrome," fitting for a breakup record built on vintage synths and syncopated grooves.
albums.reception: The album charted in a dozen countries, including France, Belgium, and Switzerland, and helped carry the band to a first Coachella appearance in 2022.
